Chapter 10: The Practice of Everyday Courage — Small Steps, Big Changes.
When you think of courage, what comes to mind? Maybe you picture something dramatic—a heroic stand, or a life-altering choice. But honestly, real courage is a lot more subtle than that. It's woven into those small, everyday moments: deciding to speak up, setting a boundary, or daring to try something new. It's about being willing to be seen for who you really are—even when that feels scary.
Imagine someone who's always avoided conflict. For them, every disagreement feels threatening, every criticism hits deep. The usual habit? Stay quiet, keep the peace, avoid rocking the boat. But then, one day, in a meeting, they decide to share what they really think. Their voice might tremble, their heart might race, but the words come out anyway. And guess what? The world doesn't end. In fact, something different starts to grow.
These tiny acts of courage—they matter more than you might think. Every time you choose to act in spite of fear, you chip away at old habits and outdated stories about who you are. Over time, you start to notice a shift. Confidence sneaks in. The need for approval loosens its grip. Life stops being about just avoiding pain, and starts being about opening up to new possibilities.
Most of the time, other people won’t even notice these moments. They might seem ordinary, even forgettable. But really, they're the bricks that build a new kind of life. Having the courage to be disliked isn't about banishing fear—it's about moving forward even when you're afraid. It's about choosing honesty over comfort, growth over safety, and being true to yourself instead of chasing approval.
In your everyday life, this could look like apologizing when you've made a mistake. Or reaching out for help when you need it. Sometimes, it's as simple as saying no to something that just doesn't feel right. It could mean trying something outside your comfort zone, or letting go of an old habit that no longer serves you. Each of these choices is a small, powerful step toward freedom.
The path never really ends—there will always be new fears, fresh challenges, and more chances to be brave. But every step counts. Every honest conversation, every moment you're vulnerable, every time you choose to show up as yourself—these are all victories.
And over time, you'll see those small steps add up to something big. A life that used to be shaped by fear, by the need to please, by the weight of the past—suddenly, it starts to feel open and free. In the end, the courage to be disliked is really the courage to live fully. To show up. To try. To care. And most of all, to be yourself.
